content: Title 21 of the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) governs the regulation of food and drugs in the United States. It is enforced by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), and the Office of National Drug Control Policy (ONDCP). Title 21 is divided into three chapters: 1. Chapter I pertains to the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). 2. Chapter II pertains to the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA). 3. Chapter III pertains to the Office of National Drug Control Policy (ONDCP). Chapter I: Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Most of the regulations in Chapter I are derived from the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. Specific areas of regulation include: Nutrition Facts Labeling: Section (c)(2)(ii): Requires the inclusion of trans fat values on nutrition labels. Section (c)(8)(iv): Requires the inclusion of vitamin and mineral values on nutrition labels. Infant Formula: Sections 106-107: Outline specific requirements for infant formula. Current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMPs) for Food Products: Section 110 et seq.: Establishes cGMPs for food manufacturing. Food Additives: Section 170: Covers regulations for food additives. Dietary Supplements: Section 190: Covers regulations for dietary supplements. Pharmaceutical Regulations (200 and 300 Series) Drug Advertising and Marketing: Sections 202-203: Regulate the advertising and marketing of drugs. Current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMPs) for Pharmaceuticals: Section 210 et seq.: Establishes cGMPs for pharmaceutical products. New Drug Requirements: Section 310 et seq.: Specifies requirements for the approval of new drugs. Over-the-Counter (OTC) Drugs: Section 328 et seq.: Details specific requirements for OTC drugs. Animal Feeds and Medications (500 Series) Animal Feeds and Medications: Section 510 et seq.: Includes regulations for animal feeds and medications, such as vaccines and blood products. Human Blood and Blood Products (600 Series) Licensing: Section 601: Covers licensing under Section 351 of the Public Health Service Act. Current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMPs) for Blood Products: Section 606 et seq.: Establishes cGMPs for human blood and blood products. Cosmetics (700 Series) Labeling Requirements: Section 701: Specifies labeling requirements for cosmetics. Medical Devices (800 Series) Medical Device Reporting: Section 803: Covers reporting requirements for medical devices. Quality System Regulations: Section 820 et seq.: Establishes quality system regulations for medical devices, which are analogous to cGMPs but structured similarly to ISO standards. Device Listings and Classifications: Section 860 et seq.: Provides a listing of specific approved devices and their classifications. Mammography and Radiation-Emitting Products (900 Series) Mammography Quality Standards: Section 900 et seq.: Covers quality requirements for mammography, enforced by the Center for Devices and Radiological Health (CDRH). Radiation-Emitting Products: Includes requirements for products such as lasers and cell phones, enforced by the CDRH. Miscellaneous Regulations (1200 Series) Public Health Service Act Regulations: Section 1240: Includes rules promulgated under Section 361 of the Public Health Service Act, which address the interstate control of communicable diseases. Examples include: Requirements for the pasteurization of milk. Regulations on the interstate shipment of turtles as pets. Regulations on the interstate shipment of African rodents that may carry monkeypox. Current Good Tissue Practices (cGTPs): These regulations pertain to the handling and processing of human cells, tissues, and cellular and tissue-based products.
